questions.q: What role does the Streaming API play relative to platform events and CDC events?
options: It defines what fields a platform event can have
It replaces the need to enable Change Data Capture
It is the transport layer that delivers those event messages over a long-lived connection, rather than defining the event types themselves
It only works with custom objects, not platform events
questions.explain: Platform events and CDC define what gets published; the Streaming API (CometD-based) is the transport that actually delivers those messages to subscribers.

questions.q: What protocol does CometD implement, and what is CometD itself?
options: CometD implements gRPC; it's a binary messaging format
CometD implements the Bayeux protocol; it's a scalable HTTP-based event-routing implementation of it
CometD implements REST; it's a JSON serialization library
CometD implements SOAP; it's an XML schema validator
questions.explain: Bayeux is the underlying asynchronous-messaging protocol, and CometD is the scalable HTTP-based implementation of it that Salesforce's Streaming API servers run.

options: The client asks "anything new?" every few seconds and gets an immediate empty response each time
A technique where the server pushes data without any request from the client at all
A batch job that runs once a day to collect all events
The server holds a client's request open until an event occurs (or a timeout), then responds, and the client immediately reconnects
questions.explain: Long polling holds the request open server-side until something happens, then responds — the client immediately re-requests, keeping a request perpetually waiting for the next event.

questions.q: What must happen before a CometD client can subscribe to a channel?
options: Nothing; subscribe can be called at any time
A successful handshake must occur first
The client must first publish at least one event
The org must disable Change Data Capture
questions.explain: The handshake is the required first step of a CometD session — subscribing and connecting both depend on a handshake having already succeeded.

questions.q: After an unexpected network disconnect and a successful CometD reconnect, what must the client do?
options: Nothing; its original subscriptions remain active automatically
Wait 72 hours before subscribing again
Switch to the Pub/Sub API, since CometD cannot recover from disconnects
Resubscribe to its channels, because a rehandshake clears previous subscriptions
questions.explain: A rehandshake after an unexpected disconnect clears prior subscriptions, so the client must resubscribe to its channels before it will receive events again.
